findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed two bowls of a green dressing in the reach in cooler dated 8/2 and numerous pans of Italian beef in the walk in cooler that had been made over the past couple days that were not date marked with the date of preparation. Date mark all ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods with the date of preparation and hold no longer than 7 days maximum (Day 1 counts as the day it is prepared). 2) Observed numerous pans of Italian beef in the walk in cooler that are probed at internal temperatures of 45F with a recently calibrated digital thermometer. Some pans were made a couple days ago and some pans were made yesterday at the end of the day and placed in the walk in cooler to cool overnight. It is unknown whether cooling occurred properly as there are no cooling logs available; therefore, it is unknown how long the food was in the temperature danger zone. Other items in this walk in cooler are 38F. If facility chooses to use this Italian beef, staff must ensure that it is reheated to 165F or above. Potentially hazardous foods must be held at 41F or below at all times.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. findings.comment: CORRECTED: Observed the sanitizer bucket reading a 0ppm concentration of Quat solution. Manager informed inspector about towels the facility purchases called Sertun.
